records.literal_gloss: And were finished the heavens and the earth and all their host.

en.L: And the heavens and the earth were finished, and all their host.
en.B: So the heavens and the earth were completed, with everything in them.
en.R: So God finished making the heavens and the earth and everything in them.

decisions.choice: all their host: everything that fills them
decisions.reason: The word means an army, or any great ordered company. Here it gathers up everything that fills the heavens and the earth: the lights and stars of the sky (Deuteronomy 4:19 calls them "the host of heaven") and all that lives on the earth.
The passive does not say who finished them, but verse 2 does: God completed his work. The verb means brought to completion, with nothing lacking.

decisions.choice: 2:1-3 closes the account of the seven days
alternatives: the start of a new section with chapter 2
decisions.reason: Chapter divisions were added to the Bible in the Middle Ages. These three verses belong with chapter 1: they close the account of the seven days, and "the heavens and the earth" recalls its first verse. In the Hebrew manuscripts the paragraph break comes after verse 3.
Readable names God as the one who finished, as verse 2 does (m2).

source.text: וַיְכַ֤ל אֱלֹהִים֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מְלַאכְתּ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה וַיִּשְׁבֹּת֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מִכָּל־מְלַאכְתּ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: And completed God on the day the seventh his work which he had done, and he rested on the day the seventh from all his work which he had done.

en.L: And on the seventh day God completed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested on the seventh day from all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done.
en.B: On the seventh day God brought to an end the work {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been doing, and on the seventh day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stopped all the work {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done.
en.R: When the seventh day came, God had finished {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work. So on the seventh day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested from all the work {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been doing.

decisions.choice: completed on the seventh day: the seventh day is the end of the work, not more work
alternatives: God still did some work on the seventh day
decisions.reason: Read on its own, the first half could suggest that God was still working on the seventh day. The second half says what completing meant: on that day God rested. Finishing the work and ceasing from it are one act, and the seventh day is the completion of the week.

decisions.choice: on the seventh day, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: on the sixth day (Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint, Syriac)
decisions.reason: The Samaritan Pentateuch, the Septuagint and the Syriac read "on the sixth day", probably so as not to suggest that God worked on the seventh. The Hebrew text, the harder reading, is followed here (m1).

The verb means to stop or cease, and the word Sabbath comes from it. God does not rest because he is tired (Isaiah 40:28); he stops because the work is complete. Exodus 20:11 and 31:17 make this the pattern for Israel's Sabbath.

decisions.choice: work: a task, especially skilled work
decisions.reason: The word is used for skilled work such as the making of the tabernacle (Exodus 36:1-2), and for the work that is not to be done on the Sabbath (Exodus 20:9-10).

Balanced says "brought to an end" and "stopped" so that the sentence does not seem to say that God worked on the seventh day (m1, m3). Literal keeps "completed" and "rested", and Readable says "had finished" and "rested".

source.text: וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־י֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י וַיְקַדֵּ֖שׁ אֹת֑וֹ כִּ֣י ב֤וֹ שָׁבַת֙ מִכָּל־מְלַאכְתּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁר־בָּרָ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And blessed God the day the seventh and made holy it, because on it he rested from all his work which created God to make.

en.L: And God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested from all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work that God had created to make.
en.B: God blessed the seventh day and set it apart as holy, since on that day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested from all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work, all that God had created and made.
en.R: God blessed the seventh day and made it a holy day. On that day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested from all the work {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done in creating the world.

decisions.choice: made holy: set apart as belonging to God
decisions.reason: To make something holy is to set it apart for God. The first thing in the Bible that God makes holy is a day, not a place or an object. Israel is later told to keep the Sabbath holy for this reason (Exodus 20:8-11).

decisions.choice: which God created to make: all the work God did in creating
alternatives: which God created so that it would go on making
decisions.reason: The words "created" and "to make" are joined to sum up the whole of God's work. The phrase closes the account with both of its main verbs: "create" (verses 1, 21, 27) and "make" (verses 7, 16, 25, 31).

decisions.choice: the seventh day has no evening and morning
decisions.reason: Each of the six days ends with "there was evening and there was morning". The seventh does not: the account ends with the day God blessed and made holy. Hebrews 4:3-10 draws on this to speak of God's rest as still open to his people.

decisions.choice: that God had created to make
alternatives: that God had created and made
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "created to make" (m2); Balanced says "created and made".
Balanced adds "set apart" to say what "holy" means (m1).
